data.text:
My weekly read of quantum research, in plain English: logical qubits did logic on $IBM and $QNT machines, and I trace what each step really cost.

Discarded runs, decoders, wires. Every claim links its paper ↓ https://t.co/LoFKF3fcrz

Qubit counts, gate fidelities, one-off demos: each tells part of the story, but none gives a holistic picture of what a quantum computer can actually compute.

Meet QUOPS (Quantum Universal Operation Performance System), a new benchmark developed by @SandiaLabs. It measures https://t.co/nvFLr340N7

⚛️ THE QUANTUM FRONTIER #007

Physical vs. Logical Qubits 

A quantum computer with 1,000 qubits isn't automatically better than one with 100.

Why?

🔹 Physical qubits = the actual hardware. Powerful, but vulnerable to errors.

🔹 Logical qubits = quantum information protected

A logical qubit was just measured on its own inside a QLDPC code block, on real hardware.

A team including UCL and the UK's NQCC ran QLDPC surgery on a [[10,2,3]] generalised bicycle code on Quantinuum's H2-2.

Single-round measurement of logical X1: 0.72% error.
Three rounds of https://t.co/5KhphXzlkK

Quantinuum ($HON) cut ion-trap logical qubit measurement error to 0.72% using generalized bicycle codes—crossing the critical 1% fault-tolerance threshold and slashing physical qubit overhead compared to standard surface codes.

Quantinuum + Sandia ran the first full tomography of a universal logical gate set: 1 logical qubit in 7 ions on H1, T gate included.
After QEC, errors looked mostly random; an emulator also caught small coherent over-rotations (arXiv). @QuantinuumQC @SandiaLabs #QuantumComputing https://t.co/zmnMHcRtiP

urls.description: We give an exact-arithmetic case study of maximum-likelihood (ML) stabilizer decoding under uncertain dephasing, separating channel-adaptive, fixed deterministic, and fixed randomized recovery decisions. For the five-qubit [[5,1,3]] code, we enumerate syndrome–stabilizer-coset masses and certify the homogeneous dephasing success polynomial 1 − 10t³ + 15t⁴ − 6t⁵. On the full homogeneous interval, adaptive ML has robust success 1/2, every fixed deterministic syndrome decoder has worst-case success zero, and fixed randomization attains 1/2. For a heterogeneous but conditionally independent family with site rates (t, t, 2t, 2t, 2t), 0 ≤ t ≤ 1/2, we obtain four algebraic switching thresholds and an exact five-piece adaptive ML curve. The adaptive and optimal fixed randomized worst-case success both equal 3/4, whereas the best fixed deterministic decoder has success min₀≤ₜ≤₁⁄₂ (16t⁵ − 28t⁴ + 10t³ + 3t² − 2t + 1) ≈ 0.749591899.
